Zadex requires WordPress 6.5 or later an: Zadex requires WordPress 6.5 or later and PHP 8.0 or later. This documentation covers Zadex 0.1.1. All described builders and elements are included in the free plugin.
You need a WordPress account allowed to: You need a WordPress account allowed to install plugins. Editing access is controlled separately by WordPress permissions and Zadex Role Manager.
In WordPress, open Plugins → Add New Plu: In WordPress, open Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for Zadex.
Install the Zadex plugin and activate it: Install the Zadex plugin and activate it. If you already have an official plugin ZIP, use Upload Plugin instead, then activate it.
Open the Zadex settings page in the Word: Open the Zadex settings page in the WordPress dashboard. Check that the content type you want to edit is enabled; posts and pages are enabled by default.
Create or open a page and choose Edit wi: Create or open a page and choose Edit with Zadex.
The editor should open around the real p: The editor should open around the real page, with your theme visible. An empty page offers a column structure for its first section. If the edit button is missing, follow the editor-access troubleshooting guide.
Requirements, installation and the setti: Requirements, installation and the settings to check before your first page.
Open a page with Edit with Zadex. Use th: Open a page with Edit with Zadex. Use the + between sections or Add section at the end of the page.
Choose a column structure. Start with on: Choose a column structure. Start with one column for a heading, description and button, or use the starter section library.
Drag Heading, Text and Button into the c: Drag Heading, Text and Button into the container. Select each element to edit its content.
Double-click supported text on the page: Double-click supported text on the page to edit inline, or use the Content panel. Give the button a label and a destination.
Use Style for typography, colors and app: Use Style for typography, colors and appearance. Use Advanced → Layout for spacing and sizing.
Prefer a shared global color or font for: Prefer a shared global color or font for repeated brand choices.
Preview the desktop, tablet and mobile l: Preview the desktop, tablet and mobile layouts. Adjust only the device values that need an override.
Use Preview mode to inspect the page wit: Use Preview mode to inspect the page without editing tools. Check text, images and destinations.
Save the page. Choose a draft or publish: Save the page. Choose a draft or published state intentionally, and confirm the save status before leaving. Open the public page to check the result.
The website playground is an illustratio: The website playground is an illustration. Actual editing, saving and publishing happen inside your WordPress installation.
Create a simple page, make it responsive: Create a simple page, make it responsive and publish it deliberately.
The real page is the canvas: The real page is the canvas
Zadex edits the real WordPress page insi: Zadex edits the real WordPress page inside your theme. Select an element on the canvas to show its controls. Its toolbar offers parent selection, moving, duplication, column splitting where applicable and deletion.
Right-click an element for copy, paste,: Right-click an element for copy, paste, style transfer, duplicate, delete, save as template and save as component actions. Actions can be restricted by a lock or your access mode.
Content changes what the element says or: Content changes what the element says or displays. Style changes its visual presentation. Advanced holds shared layout, positioning, responsive visibility, attributes, motion and display rules. The exact controls depend on the element.
Open Navigator to inspect the element tr: Open Navigator to inspect the element tree. Select the row for the element you need, including elements that are difficult to reach on the canvas.
Rename rows to describe their purpose. D: Rename rows to describe their purpose. Drag rows to reorder them; use hide and lock controls when organizing the design.
Use Ctrl+K, or Command+K on macOS, for q: Use Ctrl+K, or Command+K on macOS, for quick search. The keyboard shortcuts guide lists other verified commands.
Find your way around the editor: Find your way around the editor
The canvas, element panels, Navigator an: The canvas, element panels, Navigator and quick search.
A Container provides a Flexbox layout an: A Container provides a Flexbox layout and can act as a section or a nested column. Grid provides explicit rows and columns. Tabs, Accordion, Toggle and Off-Canvas provide nested content areas with their own interaction.
Use the section + control to choose from: Use the section + control to choose from 12 column structures, including unequal column ratios.
Drag elements between containers or arra: Drag elements between containers or arrange them in Navigator. Select the parent container when you need to edit the whole section.
Use the split action on an existing sect: Use the split action on an existing section to change its column structure while keeping its content. A single Undo restores that split operation.
Padding adds space inside an element. Ma: Padding adds space inside an element. Margin adds space outside it. Gap sets spacing between children in the layout. Start by adjusting the container rather than adding many empty spacer elements.
Preview narrow devices after changing wi: Preview narrow devices after changing width, minimum height, column ratios or positioning. Fixed dimensions can be inappropriate on smaller screens.
Choose a structure and control space wit: Choose a structure and control space without rebuilding the content.
Select the element and finish its Conten: Select the element and finish its Content settings first. Controls can appear or disappear depending on other selections.
In Style, choose typography, foreground: In Style, choose typography, foreground and background colors, borders, shadows and the other controls provided for that element.
Where a control supports hover or a devi: Where a control supports hover or a device override, choose that state or device before editing its value.
Layout covers dimensions and spacing. Po: Layout covers dimensions and spacing. Position controls placement and stacking. Responsive controls hide an element on selected devices. Motion and display conditions have dedicated guides.
Attributes accepts an ID, CSS class name: Attributes accepts an ID, CSS class names and supported attributes. Script-capable attributes are rejected. IDs should be meaningful and unique on the page.
Use the design controls for appearance. Zadex does not provide a custom CSS or JavaScript entry feature. The HTML element accepts permitted markup and removes unsafe scripting content; it is not a place to execute scripts.
Work with typography, positioning, visib: Work with typography, positioning, visibility and safe attributes.
Up to seven devices are available: mobil: Up to seven devices are available: mobile, large mobile, tablet, large tablet, laptop, desktop and widescreen. Manage enabled devices and widths in the Zadex dashboard settings.
Desktop is the base. Smaller device brea: Desktop is the base. Smaller device breakpoints use max-width; widescreen uses min-width. Do not assume a preview label is an exact physical device size.
Set your initial layout on desktop. Swit: Set your initial layout on desktop. Switch to another enabled device in the editor.
Inspect a responsive control. A faded in: Inspect a responsive control. A faded inherited value comes from a broader applicable setting, rather than an explicit value on that device.
Enter a device value only when needed. R: Enter a device value only when needed. Remove the explicit override to return to inheritance, using the control’s reset capability where available.
Check typography, gaps, column flow and: Check typography, gaps, column flow and device visibility on every enabled layout. Then inspect the public page at different browser widths.
Understand the desktop base, inherited v: Understand the desktop base, inherited values and device-specific overrides.
Set shared colors, fonts and spacing: Set shared colors, fonts and spacing
Open Site settings and define your Globa: Open Site settings and define your Global colors, Global fonts and Spacing variables.
Apply these shared choices in compatible: Apply these shared choices in compatible element controls instead of entering a separate local value each time.
Change a shared value and preview the el: Change a shared value and preview the elements using it. Local overrides can prevent a particular element from following the shared value.
A global class lets you maintain a reusa: A global class lets you maintain a reusable style and apply it to multiple elements. Class import and export support moving a style collection between projects. Use descriptive names so a teammate can recognize the purpose.
Theme style provides shared presentation: Theme style provides shared presentation for headings, buttons, links and forms. Site layout defines content width and default container gaps. Check these defaults before compensating with many element-level adjustments.
Create a consistent design system that c: Create a consistent design system that can change in one place.
Confirm that your work is saved: Confirm that your work is saved
Use Save, or Ctrl+S / Command+S, and wai: Use Save, or Ctrl+S / Command+S, and wait for the status to confirm success. Choose the intended draft or publishing state. A save error is not confirmation that the latest work reached the server.
Undo and Redo navigate editing changes,: Undo and Redo navigate editing changes, and History helps you inspect those steps. Saved Revisions are persisted versions of the page that you can return to later. They serve a different purpose from an in-session undo stack.
Before restoring a revision, save any cu: Before restoring a revision, save any current work you want to keep.
Open Revisions, inspect the available ve: Open Revisions, inspect the available version and restore the intended one. Recheck the page and save the restored design when required.
Deactivating Zadex stops rendering its l: Deactivating Zadex stops rendering its layouts but retains saved designs. The page shows its normal WordPress content, which can be empty. Reactivating Zadex makes its saved designs render again.
Understand Undo, History, saved revision: Understand Undo, History, saved revisions and deactivation.
Theme Builder supports header, footer, s: Theme Builder supports header, footer, single, archive, search, 404, loop-item and popup templates. WooCommerce adds product and shop templates when it is active. Theme parts are different from a normal page design.
Open Zadex → Theme Builder in the dashbo: Open Zadex → Theme Builder in the dashboard and create the template type you need.
Design it in the editor. In a single-con: Design it in the editor. In a single-content template, use dynamic elements such as Post title and Post content so each post supplies its own data.
Set display conditions for the whole sit: Set display conditions for the whole site or specific pages, content types, taxonomies or archives. Use exclusions where needed.
Save the template, then test a URL that: Save the template, then test a URL that should match and a URL that should not. Avoid assigning competing templates to the same destination unintentionally.
Zadex supports classic and block themes,: Zadex supports classic and block themes, including theme-part replacement. Canvas and Full Width page templates are available for page layouts. Transparent and sticky headers have additional behavior settings.
Design headers, footers, content templat: Design headers, footers, content templates and their display rules.
Element display conditions control the v: Element display conditions control the visibility of an individual element. Theme Builder display rules choose where a template is applied. A popup also has targeting and frequency rules; changing one kind of rule does not replace the others.
Select the element and open Advanced → D: Select the element and open Advanced → Display conditions, or open the template’s display rules in Theme Builder.
Choose the supported rule: user role, lo: Choose the supported rule: user role, login state, date and time, page context, URL value or dynamic field, as appropriate.
Choose the comparison and value offered: Choose the comparison and value offered for that rule. Review whether your conditions must match together or in an alternative group where the interface provides that choice.
Test with both matching and non-matching: Test with both matching and non-matching contexts, including a logged-out browser where relevant.
Display visibility is a presentation fea: Display visibility is a presentation feature. Do not use it as a replacement for access control over private WordPress content.
Show an element or template only in the: Show an element or template only in the intended context.
Entrance Motion animates an element when: Entrance Motion animates an element when it appears. Motion effects provide scroll and mouse effects such as parallax, opacity, blur, rotation, scale and 3D tilt. Scroll animation links keyframes to page scrolling. Interactions use triggers and timelines to coordinate actions.
Select the element and open its Interact: Select the element and open its Interactions controls in Advanced.
Choose a trigger such as page load, elem: Choose a trigger such as page load, element visibility, hover or click. Add the supported timeline actions and configure their timing.
Use supported actions such as animation,: Use supported actions such as animation, class changes, showing or hiding an element, or opening a popup. Preview the complete sequence.
Sticky keeps an element at the top or bo: Sticky keeps an element at the top or bottom while scrolling, and can apply appearance changes after a scroll threshold. Check the containing layout and preview the result on mobile so the sticky element does not cover essential content.
Choose the right kind of animation for t: Choose the right kind of animation for the behavior you need.
Sources include post title, excerpt, con: Sources include post title, excerpt, content, date, author, permalink, taxonomies, featured image and comment count; site name, logo, URL and description; user and archive data; current date; URL values; and custom fields.
Integrations with ACF, Pods, Toolset and: Integrations with ACF, Pods, Toolset and Meta Box are available when the corresponding plugin is installed. A dynamic control must support the value type you want to bind, such as text, image, URL, number or color.
Select an element and find a control wit: Select an element and find a control with dynamic-data support. Choose the dynamic source.
Select the field or property, and provid: Select the field or property, and provide any required custom-field key. Configure supported fallback or formatting options where offered.
Preview with a content item that actuall: Preview with a content item that actually has that data. Also check an item with an empty field so your layout handles missing content.
Connect an element to WordPress data ins: Connect an element to WordPress data instead of repeating static text.
Create a Loop item template in Theme Bui: Create a Loop item template in Theme Builder.
Build the item with dynamic fields such: Build the item with dynamic fields such as title, featured image, excerpt and permalink. Avoid typing the same fixed article title into the template.
Save the template, insert Loop Grid or L: Save the template, insert Loop Grid or Loop Carousel into a page, and choose the loop item.
Configure the query for the intended con: Configure the query for the intended content type and taxonomy restrictions. Set ordering and the number of items. Depending on the element, pagination, Load more or infinite loading are available.
Taxonomy Filter provides visitor-driven: Taxonomy Filter provides visitor-driven filtering without a full-page reload. Connect it to the appropriate loop using its controls, then test every filter and the unfiltered state. Alternate loop templates can style designated positions, such as every third item, differently.
Test an empty query, a long title and a: Test an empty query, a long title and a missing featured image. If no items appear, verify the content type, published content, filters and dynamic preview context before changing the design.
Design one item, then display real posts: Design one item, then display real posts or products in a repeatable layout.
Create a Popup template and edit its con: Create a Popup template and edit its content. Choose a centered, side, fullscreen, top-bar or bottom-bar layout.
Configure dimensions, overlay, close but: Configure dimensions, overlay, close button, entry and exit motion, scrolling behavior and automatic closing where needed.
Available triggers include a time delay,: Available triggers include a time delay, scroll progress or an element reached, click, inactivity, exit intent and ad-block detection. Popups can also be opened by supported button actions, form actions or a countdown end action.
Review page or visit thresholds, referra: Review page or visit thresholds, referral source, login state, device restrictions, maximum impressions and the wait after dismissal. A popup can be correctly designed but intentionally suppressed by one of these rules.
Save the popup and its rules. Test a qua: Save the popup and its rules. Test a qualifying visit, close the popup and check that dismissal behavior follows your configuration.
Check mobile placement and make sure the: Check mobile placement and make sure the close control remains reachable.
Separate popup design, triggering, targe: Separate popup design, triggering, targeting and frequency.
Insert the full Form element for field-l: Insert the full Form element for field-level control, or Contact Form for a simpler contact form.
Add fields, assign meaningful IDs and la: Add fields, assign meaningful IDs and labels, and choose their types and required status. Supported types include text, textarea, email, phone, number, date, time, select, radio, checkbox, acceptance, upload, password, hidden and HTML information.
Set upload restrictions through the prov: Set upload restrictions through the provided controls where applicable. Do not request information you do not need.
Configure the step structure, progress d: Configure the step structure, progress display and navigation buttons. Each step validates before progression, and the server also validates submissions. Test missing required values and invalid email input, not only the happy path.
Choose the actions you need: Email, Emai: Choose the actions you need: Email, Email 2, redirect, popup, webhook or a supported service integration. Configure each selected action; simply selecting an action does not complete its destination settings.
Use field shortcodes in supported settin: Use field shortcodes in supported settings to insert submitted values. For example, a field with ID email can be referenced as shown below.
Open Zadex → Submissions to review store: Open Zadex → Submissions to review stored messages. Mark messages read or unread, delete them when appropriate, or export CSV. Confirm the actual inbox and email delivery with a controlled test before relying on a live form.
Fields, multi-step validation, submissio: Fields, multi-step validation, submission actions and the inbox.
Set recipients, subject and message in t: Set recipients, subject and message in the selected email action. Email 2 is a separate action, useful for a different recipient or a visitor response. Review the configured sender and reply-to values and test delivery through your WordPress mail setup.
Open the Zadex dashboard settings and co: Open the Zadex dashboard settings and configure the credentials required by your chosen email service. Keep secret credentials in the provided settings, not in public page text.
In the Form element, add the service act: In the Form element, add the service action and select its destination list or audience and field mapping where provided.
Supported services include Mailchimp, Ac: Supported services include Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, GetResponse, Kit / ConvertKit, MailerLite and Drip. Slack and Discord notification actions use their configured destinations.
Send a controlled test and inspect the r: Send a controlled test and inspect the receiving service. A success message on the page alone does not prove every external action reached its destination.
Use a webhook action for a receiving end: Use a webhook action for a receiving endpoint such as an automation in Zapier, Make or n8n. Configure the URL and the action’s supported payload settings. The plugin provides automatic retries for failed webhook deliveries.
Treat an endpoint as an external destina: Treat an endpoint as an external destination: review the fields you send and confirm the receiver accepts the expected data.
Connect a form action to the right desti: Connect a form action to the right destination and verify delivery.
The form system provides a honeypot and: The form system provides a honeypot and submission rate limiting, with validation in the browser and on the server. Configure spam settings on the form and test a normal submission after changing them.
Obtain the matching reCAPTCHA v2 or v3 c: Obtain the matching reCAPTCHA v2 or v3 credentials for your site from the service.
In the Zadex dashboard settings, enter t: In the Zadex dashboard settings, enter the Site key and Secret key. Save the settings.
Enable the corresponding reCAPTCHA mode: Enable the corresponding reCAPTCHA mode in the form. Ensure the mode and domain match your service configuration, then test the public page.
reCAPTCHA is an optional external servic: reCAPTCHA is an optional external service. Its use can introduce external requests and should be reflected in your own site disclosures.
Use built-in checks and configure option: Use built-in checks and configure optional reCAPTCHA correctly.
The library includes starter sections fo: The library includes starter sections for common page structures and a complete Link in bio page. You can also save a section or page as a template and insert it later. Review inserted sample content before publishing it.
Select the part of the design you want t: Select the part of the design you want to share and use Save as component.
Insert the component in the pages that n: Insert the component in the pages that need it. Manage components from Zadex → Components and inspect where they are used.
Edit the shared component to update conn: Edit the shared component to update connected instances. Use supported instance overrides when a particular copy needs different content while keeping the rest linked.
A global widget applies the connected id: A global widget applies the connected idea to one element. Global classes share styles rather than an entire content structure. Choose a component for repeated content structure, and a class for repeated styling.
Choose between reusable content, linked: Choose between reusable content, linked components and global widgets.
Save the page you want to transfer and u: Save the page you want to transfer and use the page export capability to download its JSON.
On the destination installation, use the: On the destination installation, use the page import capability with a valid Zadex page JSON. Inspect the imported structure before publishing.
A website playground sample JSON is a de: A website playground sample JSON is a demonstration file, not a real Zadex page export.
Open Zadex → Import / Export and export: Open Zadex → Import / Export and export the site kit ZIP. Kits include pages, theme templates, global settings and images.
On the destination site, import the kit: On the destination site, import the kit and review the choices offered by the importer. Links are adjusted for the destination.
Check media, page URLs, menus, template: Check media, page URLs, menus, template rules and global styles after import. Reconfigure external services for the destination as needed.
A kit is not a full hosting backup. Keep: A kit is not a full hosting backup. Keep an independent site backup before an import that could change existing content or settings.
Move a page as JSON or transfer a comple: Move a page as JSON or transfer a complete site kit.
Open Zadex → Custom Fonts. Add the famil: Open Zadex → Custom Fonts. Add the family and upload its available WOFF2, WOFF or TTF files.
Assign the correct weight and style to e: Assign the correct weight and style to each variation so regular, bold and italic do not point to the wrong file.
Save, then select the font in the editor: Save, then select the font in the editor or assign it through Global fonts. Check that the actual font includes the scripts your site uses.
Connect an Adobe Fonts project ID from C: Connect an Adobe Fonts project ID from Custom Fonts when you choose to use that service. This differs from locally uploaded font files and depends on the external project being available.
Use or upload an icon set: Use or upload an icon set
Font Awesome Free icons are bundled. For: Font Awesome Free icons are bundled. For a custom set, open Zadex → Custom Icons and upload a supported collection from Fontello, IcoMoon or Fontastic, then choose it from compatible icon controls.
Upload brand assets and use them from th: Upload brand assets and use them from the editor.
Role Manager supports No access, Content: Role Manager supports No access, Content only and Full access for WordPress roles. Content-only editing permits supported text, image and link changes without opening design and structure controls. Restrictions are also checked on the server.
Open Zadex → Role Manager with an accoun: Open Zadex → Role Manager with an account allowed to manage these settings.
Assign the intended mode to each role. T: Assign the intended mode to each role. Test using an account with that role rather than relying on what an administrator sees.
Element locks help protect selected desi: Element locks help protect selected design areas. A locked element or restricted role can make an editor action unavailable even though that capability exists in Zadex. Check both before treating a disabled control as a defect.
Attach a note to an element, add replies: Attach a note to an element, add replies and use @mentions to notify teammates by email. Resolve a completed thread or reopen it if work continues. A note is review feedback, not a change to the page’s visitor-facing content.
Give teammates the editing scope they ne: Give teammates the editing scope they need and keep feedback on the design.
WooCommerce must be installed and active: WooCommerce must be installed and active for its Zadex elements and template types to appear. Create and configure products in WooCommerce; a page-builder product element displays that data rather than replacing product management.
In Theme Builder, create a product templ: In Theme Builder, create a product template. Add Product Title, Product Images, Product Price, stock, rating, metadata and Add To Cart as needed.
Use Product Data Tabs, Related Products: Use Product Data Tabs, Related Products or Upsells to extend the page, and set template display conditions for the intended products.
Preview products with different prices,: Preview products with different prices, stock states and image collections.
Available elements include Products, Pro: Available elements include Products, Product Categories, Cart, Checkout, My Account, Menu Cart and Purchase Summary. Review links between the shop, product, cart and checkout pages on a configured WooCommerce installation.
The website’s store simulations do not c: The website’s store simulations do not create orders or process payments. Test your actual WooCommerce configuration separately before accepting customers.
Product templates, shopping pages and th: Product templates, shopping pages and the 18 conditional store elements.
Add the PayPal button element and config: Add the PayPal button element and configure the account or destination and the supported action, amount and currency controls shown in its reference. The button relies on the PayPal service and the account configuration.
Stripe supports a payment-link destinati: Stripe supports a payment-link destination and a server-created Checkout flow. For Checkout mode, configure the Stripe secret key in Zadex dashboard payment settings; the key remains server-side. Set the button’s supported amount, currency and destination options.
Do not place a secret key in a link, cus: Do not place a secret key in a link, custom attribute or page text. Confirm account settings and use the provider’s testing facilities before enabling live payments.
Check the selected action, currency and: Check the selected action, currency and expected return destination. A visible button or the website’s illustrative payment preview does not prove a charge was processed. Verify transactions in the actual provider account.
Configure a real payment destination rat: Configure a real payment destination rather than treating a preview as a transaction.
Site settings include global styling, la: Site settings include global styling, layout, breakpoints, image lightbox, page transitions and loading appearance. Floating buttons provide contact destinations such as WhatsApp, phone and email, or a return-to-top action.
Enable a maintenance or coming-soon page: Enable a maintenance or coming-soon page
Create the page you want visitors to see: Create the page you want visitors to see, then select it in the maintenance or coming-soon settings.
Choose which roles are allowed to keep v: Choose which roles are allowed to keep viewing the normal site.
Test both an allowed signed-in account a: Test both an allowed signed-in account and a logged-out browser. Maintenance mode returns HTTP 503 to visitors and search engines.
Turn the mode off when the normal site s: Turn the mode off when the normal site should become available again.
Shared layout behavior, transitions, con: Shared layout behavior, transitions, contact buttons and maintenance pages.
Open your WordPress user profile and cho: Open your WordPress user profile and choose Arabic as the user language. Save the profile.
Reopen the Zadex editor. Its Arabic inte: Reopen the Zadex editor. Its Arabic interface and right-to-left layout follow the WordPress user language.
Changing this website’s language changes: Changing this website’s language changes the documentation and demonstrations, not your WordPress account or plugin settings.
Use a font that includes Arabic characte: Use a font that includes Arabic characters and check mixed Arabic/Latin content, navigation, icons and device overrides. Text alignment remains a design choice; translating text does not automatically settle every layout decision.
The editor offers dark mode for its inte: The editor offers dark mode for its interface. This changes the editing environment; design your page’s own colors through its element and site controls.
Change the editor language through your: Change the editor language through your WordPress user preferences.
How the page output is prepared: How the page output is prepared
Zadex generates page CSS at save time an: Zadex generates page CSS at save time and loads the generated stylesheet in the document head. Frontend scripts are loaded for features that need them, such as sliders, popups or effects. These are implementation characteristics, not a promised page-speed score.
Images, the theme, hosting, other plugin: Images, the theme, hosting, other plugins and selected external services still influence the result. Check the actual public page after saving.
When an external service is involved: When an external service is involved
The plugin does not send visitor trackin: The plugin does not send visitor tracking data to its developers. Optional services you configure can still receive data: video providers, Google Maps, SoundCloud, Facebook, Adobe Fonts, reCAPTCHA, form integrations and payment providers are examples.
Choose only the services you need and re: Choose only the services you need and reflect their actual use in your site’s privacy information. Disabling an unused integration differs from preventing an external embed already added to a page.
Understand generated styles, conditional: Understand generated styles, conditional scripts and optional connections.
Use Command in place of Ctrl on macOS. S: Use Command in place of Ctrl on macOS. Shortcuts that edit the element structure generally do not run while you are typing in an input, textarea or editable text. Save and quick search are global commands.
Select an element first for element acti: Select an element first for element actions. A locked element or a role without structural access can block duplicate, delete and paste. A browser or operating-system shortcut can also take precedence.
Verified editor commands, with Ctrl on W: Verified editor commands, with Ctrl on Windows and Command on macOS.
The searchable reference below is genera: The searchable reference below is generated from the documented plugin manifests. Each element page lists its purpose, content and style controls, available options, default values and responsive or conditional behavior.
Shared Advanced controls are explained s: Shared Advanced controls are explained separately in Style an element, Responsive design, Motion and Display conditions. WooCommerce elements appear in the editor only when WooCommerce is active.
Browse every public element and inspect: Browse every public element and inspect its actual controls.
Confirm Zadex is active and that WordPre: Confirm Zadex is active and that WordPress and PHP meet its minimum requirements.
In Zadex settings, check whether the pos: In Zadex settings, check whether the post type is enabled. A custom post type may need to be enabled explicitly.
Confirm your WordPress account can edit: Confirm your WordPress account can edit that content and that Role Manager has not assigned No access to its role.
Look for Edit with Zadex in the page lis: Look for Edit with Zadex in the page list, WordPress editor or admin bar. Reload the dashboard after changing settings.
Check activation, content types and perm: Check activation, content types and permissions before troubleshooting the page.
Read the editor’s error message and conf: Read the editor’s error message and confirm your login and permission to edit the content. Check the connection and retry Save. Keep the editor open until you have confirmed the latest work is saved; do not assume an earlier status includes your newest change.
Confirm the intended design was saved, t: Confirm the intended design was saved, then compare the same URL and device width. Check responsive overrides, element visibility, display conditions and the active Theme Builder template. If a cache layer is used, refresh its cached output through that system’s controls.
Verify the preview content has the reque: Verify the preview content has the requested field, that the source key is correct, and that an optional custom-field plugin is active. For loops, check that published records match the query and filters. For WooCommerce, confirm the plugin is active and a product context is available.
A form action did not arrive: A form action did not arrive
Confirm validation succeeded, the action: Confirm validation succeeded, the action is selected and its destination settings are complete. Check stored submissions separately from email or service delivery. Review credentials and the receiving service, and test WordPress mail delivery for email actions.
Check the saved popup template, trigger: Check the saved popup template, trigger and target page. Review device and login restrictions, impression limits and the wait after dismissal. Test a visit that meets the configured rules.
Include your Zadex, WordPress and PHP ve: Include your Zadex, WordPress and PHP versions, the relevant element or template, reproduction steps, expected and actual results, and the exact visible error. Remove secrets and personal submission data from screenshots or logs before sharing them.
Diagnose common save, display, form and: Diagnose common save, display, form and dynamic-content issues.
The documentation language could not loa: The documentation language could not load. Try again.
Try another word, or clear the search to: Try another word, or clear the search to browse all guides.
Copy the URL from your browser address b: Copy the URL from your browser address bar.
Spacing, positioning, device visibility,: Spacing, positioning, device visibility, attributes, motion and display rules are documented in the design guides.
This documentation page was not found.
Controls reflect the documented plugin v: Controls reflect the documented plugin version. Some appear only after another setting is enabled.
Open a page with Edit with Zadex, search: Open a page with Edit with Zadex, search for this element in the element panel and drag it into a container. Select it to configure the controls below.
Save your changes, preview the relevant: Save your changes, preview the relevant devices and test the element on the public page.
Practical Zadex guides, installation, ed: Practical Zadex guides, installation, editor workflows and a complete element-control reference.
Collapsible items, each a droppable cont: Collapsible items, each a droppable container. Single or multiple open, default open item, animated with full keyboard support.
